name: Anybox
tagline: A modern bookmark manager for macOS and iOS.
description:
Anybox is a bookmark manager and read-later library for Apple devices. It gives links a home outside a browser’s default bookmarks, with tags, folders, notes, screenshots, full-text context, and capture methods designed for saving a page before it disappears into an open-tab pile.

The workflow begins wherever a useful link appears. You can save the current browser tab through a shortcut, extension, menu bar item, share sheet, AppleScript, Siri Shortcut, or URL scheme, then decide later whether it belongs in a collection, needs a tag, or should simply remain searchable.

Anybox is built around a personal link library that follows you through iCloud on Mac, iPhone, and iPad. It is more structured than a browser bookmark bar, but deliberately narrower than a general database or note-taking system.

## Features

- Save links from browsers and other apps using keyboard shortcuts, extensions, the menu bar, share sheets, AppleScript, Siri Shortcuts, and URL schemes.
- Organize bookmarks with folders, tags, notes, stars, and other metadata so a saved link can be found by more than its original title.
- Use keywords to open frequent sites quickly from the address bar or a launcher-style workflow.
- Capture read-later material and current-page information in a library separate from open browser tabs.
- Sync the collection across Mac, iPhone, and iPad through the current Anybox iCloud workflow.
- Integrate with automation and launcher tools such as Alfred or Hookmark when links are part of a larger personal knowledge setup.

## Where it fits

Anybox is best for people who save many links and want a native Apple-platform library with more organization than Safari bookmarks. It works well as a dedicated inbox for articles, reference pages, product links, and recurring web resources.

It is not a full note database or collaborative bookmarking service. People who need granular exports, team sharing, or a more general-purpose knowledge system should test the current limits before moving a large archive.
